notes.meaning: David asks the Lord to bend down and listen to his cry, just as a caring parent stoops down to hear a child. He does not claim that he deserves help because of any personal greatness. Instead, he honestly brings his weakness and deep distress before God as the very reason he needs divine mercy.

David asks God to protect his life because he is sincerely devoted to the Lord and innocent of the crimes his enemies charge him with. Calling himself godly does not mean he claims to be sinless or perfect. Rather, he belongs to God, aims to show mercy to others, and puts all his confidence in the Lord alone.

David pleads for God's free favor because he knows he cannot earn it on his own. He calls out to God repeatedly throughout the entire day without giving up. Praying like this shows an ongoing trust that God will never abandon His people in their trouble.

David asks God to lift his heavy sorrow and fill his heart with true gladness. He raises his whole inner being toward heaven in sincere, trusting prayer. Believers can look forward to spiritual comfort whenever they keep their hearts closely connected to God.

David bases his hope on the loving character that God revealed to Moses at Mount Sinai. The Lord is good in His very nature, eager to forgive sins without delay, and overflowing with faithful love to all who seek Him. Knowing that God delights in pardoning gives believers courage to approach Him.

David repeats his plea for the Lord to give full attention to his desperate cry. This repetition is not an empty habit, but the heartfelt persistence of someone who deeply needs help. God is pleased when His children come back to Him again and again in earnest faith.

Troubles are certain to come, but David knows exactly where to turn when hard times arrive. He calls on the Lord with strong confidence because God has proven faithful to answer him in the past. Remembering previous answers to prayer gives us courage to ask God for help today.

David turns from his own needs to praise God for being completely unique. The lifeless idols worshipped by the heathen cannot hear cries, speak words, or perform any deeds to save people. Only the Lord has almighty power, and nothing can compare to the great works He performs.

Because God made every nation on earth, one day all people will recognize Him and bow before Him. David looks forward to a time when people everywhere leave their false gods to bring glory to the one true Lord. This points forward to the global reach of God's kingdom.
The Lord displays His supreme majesty through the wonders and miracles He works in the world. He has no rivals or partners who share His power. He alone is God over all creation.

David asks God to instruct him in His truth so he can live according to God's will. He also prays for an undivided heart, asking God to gather his scattered desires into a single focus of reverent obedience. A person cannot follow the Lord faithfully with a divided mind.

David promises to praise the Lord with the very wholehearted focus he just prayed to receive. He honors God not just as the ruler of the universe, but as his own personal Lord. His thanksgiving is not a brief reaction to good news, but a joyful commitment that will last forever.

David thanks God for His loyal, covenant love, which has rescued his life from extreme danger. In the Old Testament, Sheol refers to the grave or the realm of the dead, meaning David was brought back from the brink of physical death. Reflecting on past rescues fills the heart with gratitude toward God.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Some older Catholic writers interpreted the depths of Sheol as a reference to purgatory or an underworld compartment from which holy souls are delivered.

notes.meaning: David describes his attackers as proud, ruthless men who have teamed up to hunt him down. They act with total disregard for God and do not care about His justice. When people refuse to respect God, they quickly treat others with cruelty and violence.

David contrasts the violent cruelty of his enemies with the wonderful, gentle character of God. Echoing the words of Exodus, he remembers that the Lord is tenderly compassionate, full of unearned grace, patient with sinners, and deeply loyal to His promises. Remembering who God is brings calm and peace in the middle of a storm.

David asks the Lord to look upon him with favor and supply him with the strength he needs to keep standing. Calling himself the son of God's maidservant means he was born into God's family and household, belonging to Him from his earliest days. He appeals to this lifelong bond as a reason to trust God for protection.

David asks for a clear sign or token of God's goodness so that his enemies will see that God is protecting him and be ashamed of their plots. He does not ask this out of selfish pride, but to show that God truly cares for His faithful servants. Remembering how God helped in days past gives us hope when facing present trials.
